subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Should Gateway security owners request a private end-to-end exploit trace before accepting parse-time reserved-key filtering as a new boundary rule?
rationale: Source inspection contradicts the report's Zod and file-path premise, but only an owner-reviewed audit of method-specific handlers can conclusively rule out a downstream unsafe object-copy sink.

options.title: Triage privately first
options.body: Request a minimal payload, affected method, unsafe sink, and observed impact through private vulnerability reporting before deciding whether code hardening is warranted.

options.title: Sponsor defense-in-depth filtering
options.body: Adopt an explicit Gateway-wide reserved-key rejection policy with compatibility review and focused tests even without a demonstrated pollution sink.

recommendation.title: Triage privately first
recommendation.body: Request a minimal payload, affected method, unsafe sink, and observed impact through private vulnerability reporting before deciding whether code hardening is warranted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to the Gateway WebSocket path and repository security-reporting policy.
